name: Confluence
summary: This guide details how to set up OAuth 2.0 (3LO) authentication for Confluence by registering your own app in the Atlassian Developer Console, adding required scopes, configuring a callback URL, and completing the user authorization and token exchange flow.
decision: You must use the bring-your-own-app setup path: register your own OAuth 2.0 app in the Atlassian developer console, specify required scopes, configure your callback URL, and complete the authorization flow as outlined in the official setup instructions. No evidence is given for using a provider-managed or one-click managed credentials flow.

prerequisites.title: Atlassian Developer Account
prerequisites.body: You must have an Atlassian account to access the developer console and register apps.

prerequisites.title: Confluence Cloud site
prerequisites.body: A working Confluence Cloud site is needed to set up and authorize API access.

prerequisites.title: AWS Secrets Manager access (for AWS integrations)
prerequisites.body: AWS account with permissions to store and manage secrets if you will store credentials in AWS.

steps.title: Register a new OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app
steps.body: Sign in to the Atlassian developer console and choose 'Create', then 'OAuth 2.0 integration'. Name your app and confirm creation.

steps.title: Add required Confluence API scopes
steps.body: On the app's Permissions page, add the Confluence API and required scopes such as: read:content:confluence, read:content-details:confluence, read:space:confluence, read:space-details:confluence, read:user:confluence, read:attachment:confluence, read:page:confluence, read:blogpost:confluence, read:custom-content:confluence, and offline_access.
steps.note: Scopes listed are per integration requirements and Atlassian’s recommendations.

steps.title: Set the Callback URL
steps.body: On the Authorization page, enter a callback URL you control for code retrieval (example: https://localhost:8080/callback).

steps.title: Save Client ID and Client Secret
steps.body: On the app's Settings page, copy your Client ID and Secret for use in token exchange and credential storage.

steps.title: Authorize the application
steps.body: Open the authorization URL in a browser with your app values, sign in as an Atlassian user with content access, approve the consent prompt, and capture the authorization code from your callback endpoint.
steps.note: Example authorization URL structure provided in documentation.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
steps.body: From a terminal, POST to https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, code, and redirect_uri to receive access and refresh tokens.

steps.title: Store credentials securely
steps.body: Safely store Client ID, Client Secret, access token, and refresh token in a secure system such as AWS Secrets Manager.

steps.title: Grant permission for token rotation (if using AWS)
steps.body: Add the secretsmanager:PutSecretValue action to the relevant IAM role to enable Bedrock or connectors to rotate tokens.

human_actions.title: Register your app in Atlassian's Developer Console
human_actions.body: Go to the Atlassian developer console and create an OAuth 2.0 app for your Confluence integration.

human_actions.title: Manually set Confluence API scopes
human_actions.body: On your app's Permissions page, select and add all required scopes.

human_actions.title: Configure callback URL
human_actions.body: Set the callback URL to a location you control in your app settings.

human_actions.title: Manually perform user authorization in browser
human_actions.body: Open the constructed authorization URL, log in, approve, and retrieve the code from your callback endpoint.

human_actions.title: Exchange authorization code for tokens
human_actions.body: Use a HTTP client (e.g., curl) to POST the code and credentials to Atlassian's token endpoint and receive tokens.

human_actions.title: Store credentials and tokens securely
human_actions.body: Place credentials in a secure store such as AWS Secrets Manager for use by integrations.
